title: Kano air disaster
summary: A Boeing 707 crashed at Kano International Airport while attempting to land in high winds. The aircraft landed nose wheel first and the nose wheel collapsed after hitting a depression in the runway. The right main landing gear subsequently collapsed, the aircraft turned 180 degrees, left the runway and burst into flames. All 176 fatalities were a result of the fire.

title: Aeroflot 141
summary: Aeroflot Flight 141, a Tupolev Tu-154 with 100 occupants, crashed 1.5 kilometers short of runway 25 at Prague Ruzyně Airport on 19 February 1973. The aircraft descended below minimum safe altitude during approach and struck terrain. While most passengers initially survived the impact, a post-impact fire destroyed the fuselage and killed 62 passengers and 4 crew members. The crew reported passing the outer marker but failed to arrest descent at the required 1240 feet altitude.
probable_cause: Descent below safe altitude during instrument approach; crew failed to maintain required approach altitude.

title: Libyan Arab Airlines 114

After being intercepted by Israeli fighters, the crew was unable to receive or understand landing instructions, and the aircraft was shot down by Israeli pilot authorization.

title: Aeroflot 630
summary: An Ilyushin Il-18V operating Aeroflot Flight 630 from Dushanbe to Moscow via Leninabad crashed on 24 February 1973, killing all 79 occupants including five children. The aircraft climbed to 6,600 meters and was supposed to turn 60 degrees right toward Leninabad but instead turned only 10 degrees right, maintaining that course for three minutes with autopilot engaged. The autopilot was subsequently disengaged and the aircraft began a series of escalating bank angles, entering a steep left spiral at 90 degrees bank with vertical speeds of 100 meters per second, ultimately disintegrating from high dynamic loads at 2,200 meters altitude.
probable_cause: Navigation error and loss of control; the aircraft made an improper turn after climbing to cruise altitude, then entered an uncontrolled spiral dive from which recovery was not attempted or possible.

title: Aeroflot 6551
summary: An Ilyushin Il-18B on a scheduled flight from Baku to Novosibirsk was last contacted at 01:22 MSK reporting departure from Ayaguz sector toward Semipalatinsk. The aircraft entered an uncontrolled right bank and the right wing separated at 5,000 m. The fuselage broke apart at 3,600 m, well above the aircraft's maximum safe speed. Despite recovery of flight data recorders, investigators could not definitively determine the cause. All 63 aboard were killed.

title: 1973 Paris Air Show crash
summary: Soviet test aircraft Tupolev Tu-144S performed aerobatic maneuvers during its second demonstration flight at the 1973 Paris Air Show as part of competition with Concorde. After a high-speed pass with landing gear and canards extended at low altitude, the aircraft went into a steep rapid climb with all four engines at full power. Below 2,000 ft the aircraft stalled and fell into a steep dive. When attempting recovery at 400 ft the left wing outboard of the engines broke away. The aircraft snap-rolled, inverted, and broke apart in mid-air crashing on Goussainville with all six crew and eight ground fatalities.

The aircraft descended below the glide slope and crashed in a wooded ravine 2 miles short of the runway. summary: A Tupolev Tu-124V en route from Vilnius to Moscow entered a steep dive during descent to 5,700 meters. The flight crew lost situational awareness due to gyro failure sustained in the dive. Investigators determined that a spontaneous electrical short circuit had caused the elevator trim tab to deflect upward, initiating the dive and subsequent spin. All 51 aboard were killed.
probable_cause: A spontaneous short circuit caused the elevator trim tab to deflect to and maintain an upward position, sending the aircraft into a dive and resulting spin. The crew lost situational awareness and control due to gyro failure from loads sustained in the dive.

factors.evidence: a spontaneous short circuit had caused the elevator trim tab to deflect to and maintain an upward position
elevator trim tab to deflect to and maintain an upward position, which sent the aircraft into a dive and a resulting spin
Because of a loss of situational awareness and a gyro that had failed due to loads sustained in the dive, the crew again lost control of the airplane
the aircraft entered a steep dive and were having difficulties recovering
it then entered a stall, followed by a spin

events.text: At 19:03 MSK air traffic controllers in Moscow gave the pilots clearance to begin a descent to 5,700 m
At 19:11 MSK, the pilots reported the aircraft had entered a steep dive and were having difficulties recovering
Just 2,000 m above the ground, the pilots were able to briefly stabilize the aircraft
However, it then entered a stall, followed by a spin
At 19:13 MSK, the aircraft crashed into the ground near the village of Karacharovo, northwest of Moscow

title: 1973 Rome airport attack and hijacking
summary: On December 17, 1973, armed members of Fatah conducted a terrorist attack at Rome-Fiumicino Airport, firebombing Pan Am Flight 110 while at the gate. The airport's inadequate security design and staffing allowed gunmen to penetrate to the aircraft tarmac with automatic weapons and incendiary grenades. Fires from grenades destroyed the aircraft and killed thirty persons on board, with evacuation hampered by gunmen obstructing emergency exits. The attack exposed fundamental deficiencies in airport security infrastructure and regulatory oversight.
probable_cause: Armed terrorist attack with incendiary devices; inadequate airport security design and oversight enabled penetration to aircraft; gunmen threw grenades and small arms fire set aircraft on fire at gate.

factors.evidence: five suspects made their way through the terminal building, armed with automatic firearms and grenades, throwing incendiary grenades through the aircraft doors
airport structure was unsuitable for the prevention of terrorist attacks, as it was designed at a time when such events were rare
At the time, 117 officers were on duty at the airport with only 8 employed in the anti-sabotage service, a negligible number for an intercontinental airport
Stewardesses were able to open the emergency exit over the wing on one side; the other exit was obstructed by gunmen

events.text: Armed gunmen entered terminal and began firing throughout building with automatic firearms and grenades, killing two people in terminal
Gunmen ran across tarmac toward Pan American jet throwing phosphorus incendiary grenades through open aircraft doors
Fires from incendiary grenades spread through cabin; explosions knocked crew and passengers down; stewardesses opened emergency exit over wing but other exit was obstructed by gunmen
Aircraft destroyed by fire; twenty-nine passengers and purser Diana Perez died on the plane from fires

notes: this is a ground-based security event, not a traditional aviation accident
aircraft destroyed while at gate preparing to taxi, not in flight
separate hijacking of Lufthansa Flight 303 also occurred in same attack with two fatalities but crew was not incapacitated

title: Accidente de un Sud Aviation Caravelle de Royal Air Maroc en 1973
summary: The aircraft was a 12-year-old Sud Aviation Caravelle operated by Royal Air Maroc on a flight from Paris to Casablanca with a stopover in Tangier, carrying 98 passengers and 8 crew. During approach to runway 28 at Tangier-Boukhalef Airport at night in rainy weather, the aircraft made a delayed turn and entered a mountainous area. At 22:10 local time, the aircraft crashed into Mount Mellaline located 20 miles east of Tangier-Boukhalef Airport at an altitude of 2300-2400 ft, killing all 106 people on board.
probable_cause: The flight crew made a delayed turn during approach to Tangier-Boukhalef Airport at night in rainy weather, entering a mountainous area and descending below the assigned safe holding altitude of 3000 ft.

factors.evidence: the crew made a delayed turn and entered a mountainous area
the approach was conducted at night in rainy weather
the crew was assigned a safe holding altitude of 3000 ft but descended below this altitude
the aircraft crashed into Mount Mellaline at an altitude of 2300-2400 ft

events.text: The crew was assigned a safe holding altitude of 3000 ft during the approach to runway 28
The flight was then cleared to land and the aircraft resumed its descent
